meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 Loop pressure control needs more and more purge (Methanol Converter R-201)
meta.caseTitle: Loop pressure control needs more and more purge
meta.sit: Over the last hour the purge PV-203 has opened further to hold 75 bar g, methanol production is a few t/h lower, and bed 1 exit has fallen. Make-up flow and composition are unchanged.

0.1.unit: R-201 is the ICI-type 4-bed quench converter of a 900 kt/y methanol synthesis loop. Make-up syngas (FIC-202, 366 kNm³/h: H₂ 73, CO 16, CO₂ 7 %) joins the recycle at the C-201 circulator (FIC-201, 1928 kNm³/h); the gas is heated in E-202 and E-201 against the converter effluent, enters bed 1 at 220 °C (TIC-211 on the E-201 bypass TV-211), and cold shots TV-221/231/241 set the inlets of beds 2–4 (225/230/235 °C). The effluent is cooled in E-201, E-202 and E-203 (cooling water); V-201 separates the crude methanol (LIC-204, LV-204) from the loop gas; PIC-203 holds the loop at 75 bar g by purging gas through PV-203. Design: methanol 112.5 t/h, purge about 105 kNm³/h, outlet CH₃OH about 4.8 %.

rows.what: Purge FI-203 rose from 105.1 to 113.1 kNm³/h (peak 116.9 at 0:30:55); PV-203 opened from 45.0 to 48.4 %

Bed 1 exit TI-214 fell from 259.9 to 244.3 °C with TIC-211 on 220.0 °C

0.4.ctx: Normal shift, loop lined out at the design point; no set point, valve or make-up change was made in the last hour and the front end reports the make-up flow and composition unchanged. The case was handed over at OTS time 00:00:00; the pulled data start one hour earlier (record time 0:00:00 = OTS −01:00:00), so record time 1:00:00 is the hand-over.

R.1.p: CO + 2 H₂ ⇌ CH₃OH and CO₂ + 3 H₂ ⇌ CH₃OH + H₂O on Cu/ZnO/Al₂O₃, both exothermic and both limited by equilibrium at the bed exit temperatures. Each adiabatic bed heats up as it converts (≈ 40 °C at design); the cold shots bring the gas back down before the next bed. Only about 5 % of the converter gas becomes methanol per pass, so the loop recycles the rest; the inerts (CH₄, N₂) and any unconverted gas that the converter does not use must leave with the purge. PIC-203 holds the loop pressure by opening PV-203 whenever gas accumulates: the purge rate is the loop’s measure of how much gas the converter fails to convert.

R.2.eq: Purge ≈ make-up − (gas converted to methanol + water) − gas dissolved in the crude      ΔT_bed ≈ (−ΔH) · ξ / (F · c̄p)      r = k₀ · a · exp(−E/RT) · f(p, y)

3.2.n: Heat released XI-260 84.5 → 82.3 MW (−2.2 MW) and methanol −3.31 t/h: less reaction. Bed ΔT 39.9/51.9/40.0/32.7 → 24.3/47.6/41.1/36.5 °C: bed 1 lost 15.6 °C of rise, beds 3 and 4 gained — the top of the converter converts less and the gas reaches the lower beds less converted, where the reaction is closer to equilibrium. Unconverted CO and CO₂ accumulate (AIT-205 CO 4.88 → 5.70 %, CO₂ 3.35 → 3.92 %) and PIC-203 purges them: FI-203 +7.9 kNm³/h. CH₄ fell (9.93 → 9.27 %) because the bigger purge dilutes the inerts — inerts are not the cause.

5.1.proof: Bed ΔT 39.9/51.9/40.0/32.7 → 24.3/47.6/41.1/36.5 °C (Ev-4); AIT-205 CO and CO₂ up, CH₄ down, lab agrees (Ev-5, Ev-10); T-1 killed the instrument, leak, cooling and inert causes; T-2: bed 1 ΔT grew 24.4 → 31.8 °C for +7 °C at the inlet (Ev-14)
5.1.mech: The copper crystallites of the catalyst sinter → fewer active sites in every bed (activity a falls) → at the same inlet temperatures each bed converts less: bed 1 releases less heat (ΔT ↓) and the reaction zone moves down the converter to beds 3 and 4, which run closer to equilibrium → less methanol per pass (AIT-208 ↓) → unconverted CO and CO₂ accumulate in the loop gas → PIC-203 opens PV-203 to hold 75 bar g → purge ↑, methanol ↓, carbon lost to fuel.

5.7.n: Purge, AIT-205 CO and C-201 power moved as predicted. After 30 min: Methanol 109.24 → 110.27 t/h (+1.03), purge 112.6 → 110.2 kNm³/h, AIT-205 CO 5.66 → 5.33 %, C-201 80.0 → 88.0 % speed and 6.52 → 8.64 MW, margin 15769 → 15872 USD/h; hottest bed exit 271.7 °C; no alarm. XI-210 rose 1.03 t/h, less than the workbook's 1 % threshold (1.09 t/h), so 5.6 marks it as diverging; on the trend the rise is clear against a noise of a few hundredths, and the crude FI-209 went 127.4 → 128.9 t/h. The gain is a third of the loss, as expected: lost activity cannot be bought back with temperature and flow, only partly compensated.

5.8.rule: When the purge rises with the make-up and pressure unchanged, read the bed ΔTs before blaming the front end: a smaller ΔT at the top and a larger one at the bottom is the converter losing activity.

6.0.n: T-2 showed the predicted bed 1 response; the compensation gave +1.03 t/h and −2.4 kNm³/h of purge, meeting the SMART goal; the real fix is the catalyst change.

hyp.cause: Catalyst activity lost in every bed (ageing / sintering)
hyp.ifthen: If every bed lost activity, each converts less at the same inlet: bed 1 ΔT falls, the reaction moves down to beds 3–4, unconverted CO and CO₂ rise in the loop and the purge rises; a hotter bed 1 inlet still raises its ΔT (slow but alive)
hyp.key: ΔT bed 1 ↓, beds 3–4 ↑; AIT-205 CO, CO₂ ↑; T-2: bed 1 ΔT grows
hyp.fals: Bed ΔTs unchanged; or CH₄ rising; or bed 1 ΔT unchanged in T-2

hyp.cause: Local loss of activity in one bed (poison or fouling in one place)
hyp.ifthen: If only one part of the converter lost activity, that bed’s ΔT would change and the next bed would take up its work, while the other beds kept their shape; the dead part would hardly respond to a hotter inlet
hyp.key: One bed’s ΔT changes, the others compensate; little response to a hotter inlet
hyp.fals: All beds shift together; bed 1 responds strongly to a hotter inlet

hyp.cause: Inerts building up in the loop
hyp.ifthen: If inerts accumulated, AIT-205 CH₄ would climb and the purge would rise to carry them out
hyp.fals: CH₄ falls; lab GC CH₄ normal

hyp.cause: Loop pressure measurement wrong — PIC-203 controls on a wrong reading
hyp.ifthen: If the transmitter were wrong, the real loop pressure would differ from PIC-203 and the independent readings would show it
hyp.key: PI-201 or PG-203 disagree with PIC-203

hyp.cat: Heat exchange (E-201, E-202, E-204, E-203 & cooling water)
hyp.ifthen: If part of the gas bypassed the catalyst, the beds would keep their profile while the products fell, and samples across the exchangers would disagree
hyp.key: Bed profile unchanged; samples across E-201 differ
hyp.fals: Bed profile changed; samples across E-201 equal

hyp.cause: Separator or cooling short of design — product recycled
hyp.cat: Heat exchange (E-201, E-202, E-204, E-203 & cooling water)
hyp.ifthen: If the separator ran off design, TI-253 would move and product would return to the converter with the recycle gas
If the make-up changed, the front end’s analysis would show it and the ratio of CO to CO₂ in the loop would shift
hyp.key: Make-up analysis different; CO:CO₂ ratio shifts
hyp.fals: Front end reports no change; CO and CO₂ both rose (more unconverted gas, same ratio)

hyp.cause: Bed 1 exit thermocouple TE-214 reads low
hyp.ifthen: If only TE-214 drifted, the other bed temperatures and the purge would not move and the spare element would disagree
hyp.fals: Spare = TI-214; other tags moved too

tests.title: Field and lab round: GC converter inlet and outlet, crude, samples across E-201, TE-214 spare element, E-203 cooling water, valve walk
tests.move: Field tab ▸ send the outside operator for the seven checks at 1:10:00; nothing changed on the process.

WH-3.note: lab CH₄ above design and rising

WH-6.note: cooling water short, TI-253 off design

tests.kill: Each check kills its hypothesis when it reads normal: lab CH₄ ≤ design; samples across E-201 equal; CW ≥ 90 % flow; spare element within 2 °C of TI-214.

res.obs: Lab GC, converter inlet: H2 79.4 %, CO 5.70 %, CO2 3.92 %, CH4 9.27 %, N2 1.40 %, CH3OH 0.29 % (AIT-205 shows CO 5.71 / CO2 3.94 / CH4 9.26 %). CH3OH before E-201 4.64 %, after E-201 4.64 % (the same within the analysis error). TE-214 healthy; spare element reads 244 °C (TI-214 244 °C). CW supply 32 °C; return 41 °C; FG-203 flow gauge about 100 % of normal.

tests.title: Bed 1 inlet +7 °C: TIC-211 SP 220 → 227 °C (inside the 228 °C HI alarm)
tests.move: At 1:20:02 raise TIC-211 SP 220 → 227 °C in one step; nothing else touched; hold 20 min.

WH-1.note: by MORE than the 7 °C step: bed 1 ΔT grows (slow but active catalyst)

WH-2.note: by about the step only: a dead part of the bed does not react more

tests.kill: Direction alone cannot separate them: bed 1 ΔT grows by > 3 °C and TI-212 rises by > 1.2 × the step → WH-2 killed, WH-1 confirmed; ΔT unchanged → WH-1 killed.
tests.stop: Stop if TI-214 > 270 °C, any bed exit at its HI alarm, or TIC-211 HI

res.obs: TI-214 244.4 → 258.6 °C (+14.2) for a TIC-211 step of +6.8 °C: bed 1 ΔT 24.4 → 31.8 °C; TI-212 230.6 → 240.1 °C; purge 112.9 → 110.3 kNm³/h after 5 min, back to 112.6 after 20 min; methanol 109.13 → 109.71 → 109.24 t/h; bed 2 exit 272.6 → 269.8 °C; no alarm.
